title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E05 — The Royal Shipyards
Exploring the world of 18th-century shipyards, where large-scale organization provides a blueprint for later factory-era industrialization; how ships are made; the challenges shipbuilders face, such as fires, rot and decay.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E06 — The Textile Industry
Turning to the actual process of industrialization that begins in the textile business; surveying the work of spinning and weaving textiles; learning about several key inventors; their innovations, such as the flying shuttle and the spinning jenny.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E07 — Coal Mining
Coal mining becomes a large-scale capitalist enterprise; diving into one of the most dangerous jobs in the world; the problems miners have to overcome; examining some of the solutions; learning about steam engines, safety lamps, ventilation and more.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E08 — Iron - Coking and Puddling
Iron is an important raw material for the Industrial Revolution; the history of iron; how to produce pig iron and forge wrought iron; meeting many of the key innovators who improve the process of bringing higher-quality iron into a growing market.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E01 — A Middle East Crossroads in the Year 1900
How western imperialism, the politics of oil, and the push for a Jewish state all set the stage for the 20th century.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E02 — Constitutional Revolts in Persia and Turkey
How protests in Persia led to a new government; then why the Young Turks wanted a united Turkey to supersede the Ottoman Empire.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E03 — World War I and the Ottoman Empire's Fall
The promises of Arab and Turkish nationalism and the construction of a Jewish state collide after the war.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E04 — Egyptian Revolution and Turkish Independence
The fallout from World War I with a look at the Turkish War of Independence in 1919, as well as anti-British uprisings from Egypt to Iraq.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E05 — Monarchies of the 20th-Century Middle East
Exploring the monarchies in the Middle East and North Africa in the period between the World Wars.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E06 — The Muslim Brotherhood and Its Founder
Imam Hassan al-Banna is the founder of the Muslim Brotherhood.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E07 — World War II Fault Lines in the Middle East
A high-level look at World War II and its impact on the Middle East and North Africa.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E08 — European Anti-Semitism and Israel's Birth
Tracing the development of Israel up to the creation of the state in 1948.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — Industrialization Is Good for You
Stepping into the story of one of the greatest periods in history; investigating why people should be grateful for the Industrial Revolution, even though there is much to dislike about industrialization.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — Why Was Britain First?
Starting at the beginning in the British Isles; various factors contribute to the birth of the Industrial Revolution, including relative political stability, sophisticated financial institutions, colonial trade and a rising population of workers.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E03 — The Agricultural Revolution
In Britain in the 18th century, new agricultural methods come into being; a look at some of these changes to agriculture, including different uses of the land, the introduction of new crops and the early mechanization of farming.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E04 — Cities and Manufacturing Traditions
Traversing the country to see where industry takes off; starting with a detailed look at the advantages and dangers of life in London; shifting attention to provincial cities and towns, where industrialists face various challenges.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E01 — Pacific Crest Trail
Exploring the Pacific Crest Trail, an extraordinary route that stretches 2,650 miles from the deserts of Southern California on the Mexico border all the way to the Canadian border in Washington.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E02 — Hayduke Trail
Mick journeys along the hazardous 800-mile backcountry route of the Hayduke Trail.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E03 — Pacific Northwest Trail
Traveling one of the most scenic and rugged long-distance trails in the world: the 1,200-mile Pacific Northwest Trail.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E04 — Continental Divide Trail
At 3,100 miles, the Continental Divide Trail is the second-longest National Scenic Trail in the United States, and arguably the most rugged, remote, and hazardous of them all.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E05 — Great Allegheny Passage
Exploring a predominantly flat hiking trail from Pennsylvania's Pittsburgh to Maryland's Cumberland.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E06 — Appalachian Trail
Checking out the world's longest hiking trail, located in North America.

description:
S01 E01 — Hearing the Banjo's Journey from Africa
When studying the gourd banjo, one must consider the musical interchange that occurred between African and European cultures.

title: The Banjo: Music, History, and Heritage
description:
S01 E02 — The Banjo and the Fiddle Together
African-American string band musician Joe Thompson is known for his old-time country tunes.

title: The Banjo: Music, History, and Heritage
description:
S01 E03 — Minstrel Banjo
Inappropriate as they may be, minstrel shows occupy a significant place in the history of the banjo.

title: The Banjo: Music, History, and Heritage
description:
S01 E04 — The Spiritual Roots of the Banjo
There is a special connection between the early banjo and religious symbols.

title: The Banjo: Music, History, and Heritage
description:
S01 E05 — The Banjo in Ragtime and Jazz
Whether it is ragtime or New Orleans jazz, the banjo is a great instrument for syncopation.

description:
S01 E06 — The Irish Banjo
Giddens introduces some of the early figures associated with the Irish banjo.

title: The Banjo: Music, History, and Heritage
description:
S01 E07 — The Banjo's Evolution in Ireland
Giddens explains the evolution of gourd banjos and the development of the tambourine.

title: The Banjo: Music, History, and Heritage
description:
S01 E08 — Migration, Music, and Commercialization
The banjo is believed to have played a significant role in facilitating cross-cultural exchanges.

title: England, the 1960s, and the Triumph of the Beatles
description:
S01 E01 — The Magical Mystery of the Beatles
What happens between September 1963 and February 1964 to launch the Beatles toward international stardom; discovering some of the major social and sonic factors at work in the transformation of these young musicians into a pop culture hurricane.

title: England, the 1960s, and the Triumph of the Beatles
description:
S01 E02 — Fateful Intersections in Liverpool
The Beatles are a product of the many worlds contained within 1950s and 1960s Liverpool; how the band soaks up this post-industrial and culturally vibrant scene; how they store ideas and impressions that turn up in some of their early tunes.

description:

Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:

Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

title: America's Musical Heritage
description:

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Chess: The Evolution of a Strategy Icon
Developed during the Guptas' rule in India, Chaturanga is a strategy game resembling chess. It gradually wended its way westward to become what it is in the present.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Chess's Eastern Cousins: Shogi and Xiangqi
The East Asian games of Xiangqi and Shogi are potentially connected to Chaturanga and chess, but a lack of documentation makes it difficult to ascertain anything.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — Go: A Game of Near-Infinite Complexity
Go is an intricate strategy game that outshines chess in East Asia because of its challenging nature and unique setup.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E06 — Sowing Seeds: Africa's Mancala Family
Mancala is a family of traditional African games dating back over 7,000 years. Awari and Bao are two members that fall on opposite ends of the spectrum of difficulty.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E07 — Decoding the Past: The Royal Game of Ur
Learning about the rules and significance of the Royal Game of Ur, an ancient Sumerian game that was lost to time and resurrected through archaeological findings.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E08 — Pachisi: India's Iconic Racing Game
An enormous game board in Mughal emperor Akbar's palace courtyard bears witness to his fondness for Pachisi, a board game that has existed for ages in different forms.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E01 — What Is the Occult?
The occult, in the popular imagination, is often associated with evil, cheap magic tricks and superstitions; the world of the occult is much deeper and broader than that, encompassing an entire philosophy and way of life for some believers.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E02 — Fauns, Fairies, and Djinn
Occultism posits that people are surrounded by a hidden world inhabited by intelligent beings.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E03 — The Christmas Tree and Other Rituals
A look at the occult concepts and symbolism embedded in common religious practices across different traditions, including the Christmas tree and Santa Claus, a Native American Ghost Dance of the 19th century American West and more.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E04 — Practical Magic: Love, Money, and Health
A look at if occult techniques are just mental hacks that allow people to tap into their natural abilities; turning to the utilitarian side of occultism: practical magic.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E05 — Alchemy, Astrology, and Divination
A look at the three pillars of occultism: alchemy, astrology and ritual magic.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E06 — Talking With the Dead
Delving into the world of spirit communication and necromancy, from Stone Age shamans to Harry Houdini's anti-spiritualist crusade of the early 20th century.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E07 — The Occult Ancient World
From the late Ice Age to the 14th century, an exploration of the origins and influence of occult ideas and practices.

title: Secrets of the Occult
description:
S01 E08 — Vampires, Werewolves, and Zombies
Creatures like vampires, werewolves and zombies have become modern pop culture mainstays, but their origins are much older and more interesting than their current iterations would suggest.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Chess: The Evolution of a Strategy Icon
Developed during the Guptas' rule in India, Chaturanga is a strategy game resembling chess. It gradually wended its way westward to become what it is in the present.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Chess's Eastern Cousins: Shogi and Xiangqi
The East Asian games of Xiangqi and Shogi are potentially connected to Chaturanga and chess, but a lack of documentation makes it difficult to ascertain anything.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — Go: A Game of Near-Infinite Complexity
Go is an intricate strategy game that outshines chess in East Asia because of its challenging nature and unique setup.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E06 — Sowing Seeds: Africa's Mancala Family
Mancala is a family of traditional African games dating back over 7,000 years. Awari and Bao are two members that fall on opposite ends of the spectrum of difficulty.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E07 — Decoding the Past: The Royal Game of Ur
Learning about the rules and significance of the Royal Game of Ur, an ancient Sumerian game that was lost to time and resurrected through archaeological findings.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E08 — Pachisi: India's Iconic Racing Game
An enormous game board in Mughal emperor Akbar's palace courtyard bears witness to his fondness for Pachisi, a board game that has existed for ages in different forms.

description:

The occult, in the popular imagination, is often associated with evil, cheap magic tricks and superstitions; the world of the occult is much deeper and broader than that, encompassing an entire philosophy and way of life for some believers.

title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
description:
S01 E01 — The Journey Ahead
Cosmology takes the entire universe as its subject, not just its form, structure and contents, but also the manner of its birth and evolution; looking at the origin of cosmology in creation stories and its relation to the journey ahead.

title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
description:
S01 E02 — Denizens of the Universe
Introducing the hierarchy of structures in the universe; from planets to stars, galaxies, galaxy clusters and larger groupings of galaxies called the cosmic web; light travels at a finite speed, looking far away also means looking far back in time.

title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
description:
S01 E03 — Overall Cosmic Properties
Discussing cosmic properties; the universe is lumpy at the scale of galaxies and galaxy clusters; at larger scales, it is smooth and similar in all directions; this property of homogeneity and isotropy is called the cosmological principle.

title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
description:
S01 E04 — The Stuff of the Universe
The most familiar constituents of the universe are atomic matter and light; neutrinos make up another component; 96 percent of the universe is dark energy and dark matter; the relative amounts of these constituents changes as the universe expands.

title: The Origin and Evolution of Earth: From the Big Bang to the Future of Human Existence
description:
S01 E01 — Mineralogy and a New View of Earth
Beginning the study of Earth's history by voyaging backward in time; seeing how each crucial stage in the evolution of the planet depends on what comes before; previewing the role played by minerals, which coevolve with life.
